rows.observation: Excavator operator was traveling down a haul road when the machine veered off the road and fell over a 317-foot highwall.
Delivery truck driver was killed when his vehicle traveled off the roadway and overturned into a ravine.
Two powered haulage vehicles collided at a blind intersection in the pit area.
Miner was entangled in a belt conveyor tail pulley while cleaning material without stopping the belt.
Worker was fatally struck by shifting stock-piled material while clearing equipment at the base of the pile.
Worker crushed between conveyor belt and frame during belt tracking adjustment.
Mechanic entangled in tail pulley while adjusting belt tension on active conveyor.
Haul truck crashed through road barrier into ditch.
Miner struck by falling rock during roof support installation.
Mechanic caught between moving pulley and frame during belt check.
Haul truck struck a stationary vehicle due to blind corner speed and no traffic control.
Maintenance worker injured due to LOTO failure during mechanical equipment service.
Haul truck lost control on slick ramp and tipped over edge without berm containment.
Miner entrapped following uncontrolled shift of stored timber supplies in walkway.
Operator fatally struck by collapsing highwall during scaling operations.
Miner struck by haul truck while crossing blind intersection.
Worker entangled in rotating belt conveyor nip point.
Worker was entangled in a rotating machine shaft after the safety guard was removed for production speed.
Excavation walls collapsed during pipe installation due to failure to use a trench box in unstable soil.
Worker entered a grain bin without performing atmospheric testing and was trapped by shifting grain.
Worker was not wearing a fall harness while installing building roof metal deck, 30 feet up.
High-pressure hose leaked ammonia refrigerant; worker lacked respiratory protection in the spill area.
Forklift struck a wall because speed limit was ignored in high-traffic pedestrian walkway.
Rotating parts on milling machine lacked proper guarding.
Emergency fire exit aisle completely blocked by stacked crates.
Excavation walls failed during pipe installation; lack of shoring present.
Worker reached into press machine while in motion due to guard override.
Emergency fire exit aisle completely blocked by pallet storage.
Crane boom contacted power line while lifting heavy structural steel.
Scaffolding overloaded with concrete material collapsed, dropping two workers.
Emergency fire exit path completely obstructed by pallet inventory.
Emergency exit path completely obstructed by pallet inventory.
Scaffold setup lacking engineered base support caused collapse during use.
Installer working at 15 feet without harness system in high-exposure work zone.
Trench collapse occurred because no shoring or trench box was installed in sandy soil.
Valve failure released chemicals into work area; no containment.
Toxic vapor exposure; area lacked ventilation and cleanup.
Worker in unprotected trench without ladder.

A contractor crew was installing pipe supports inside an operating processing plant. Workers used a scaffold and grinders. The note does not clarify whether OSHA construction, OSHA general industry, or MSHA applies.

A railcar was being loaded near the mine plant boundary. The note does not confirm whether the work was under mine operations, railroad control, or contractor control. Workers were near moving rail equipment.

Coal spillage had accumulated along the beltline near a travelway. The note says miners walk through the area, but it does not confirm whether the belt was running, whether cleanup was underway, or whether guarding/lockout was needed.

A battery scoop was on charge in an underground shop. The area had a fan running, but the observation does not confirm hydrogen monitoring, charger condition, eyewash availability, or whether ignition sources were controlled.

A miner was cleaning spilled material near the tail pulley area while the conveyor was stopped. The report does not confirm whether the belt was locked out or only paused from the control room. Guarding around the pulley was partially removed.

An ore pass opening was observed near the drift. A chain was present but sagging, and the sign was dirty. The note does not confirm whether the opening was adequately barricaded or whether employees could access the edge.
A loader was parked in the yard with the bucket lowered. No pedestrians were nearby, no travel was occurring, and no backing movement was observed. The concern was an expired pre-use inspection tag.
At the dump point, the berm appeared lower than the axle height of trucks using the area. The photo is angled and does not clearly show berm continuity or truck position during dumping.

A crew planned to weld inside a tank later in the shift. At the time of inspection, the manway was open and an entrant was checking tools near the opening. No atmospheric test, permit, attendant, ventilation, or hot work authorization was documented.

Employees complained of headaches in a busy propane forklift charging and staging area with loud backup alarms. The note does not include CO readings, ventilation status, noise dosimetry, or forklift maintenance records.

A tank was labeled as a permit-required confined space, but the employee was only walking past it. No entry, partial body entry, testing, cleaning, or retrieval setup was involved in the observed condition.
Spoil material was piled near the edge of an excavation. The note does not confirm excavation depth, soil type, distance from edge, or whether workers entered the trench.
A crane boom was positioned near overhead utility lines. The observation does not confirm voltage, distance, de-energization, spotter use, or whether minimum approach distance was evaluated.

Employees were working in a trench beside a utility line. The photo shows vertical walls, but the depth, soil type, protective system, ladder access, and competent-person inspection were not documented.

Three plastic storage bins were stacked in front of an office electrical panel, blocking clear working space clearance access. The panel outer door was closed, latched, and completely intact with no damaged parts or wiring.

Temporary portable extension cords and lighting strings were in use outdoor in wet weather. No ground fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) protection devices or assured grounding program records were provided.
Pallets of finished product were staged in front of an exit door. The exit sign was visible, but the path width and whether the door could open fully were not documented.

An employee was working on an elevated platform 12 feet high. The access ladder was missing, requiring workers to climb the structural scaffolding framing to reach the platform. No trench or excavation was involved.

Forklift was parked in the shipping area and the supervisor said the operator training file could not be located. No unsafe driving, pedestrian exposure, struck-by event, or equipment defect was observed during the inspection.
The audit note says conveyor pinch point training records were incomplete. No conveyor was running, no guard was missing, and no employee exposure to moving parts was observed.

Employees were loading trailers in a hot warehouse during the afternoon. The note mentions sweating and fatigue, but no WBGT, temperature, workload, acclimatization, water access, or work-rest schedule was documented.
An employee was reaching toward a jammed packaging machine. The machine appeared stopped, but the note does not confirm whether it was locked out, blocked, or capable of unexpected movement.
A compressed air hose had cracked outer covering near a workstation. It is unclear whether the hose was pressurized, leaking, restrained, or removed from service.
A pedestal grinder had the tongue guard removed and the tool rest gap appeared excessive. The operator was wearing safety glasses, and no missing PPE was observed.

Employees were torch cutting a bracket near cardboard boxes and oily absorbent pads. The note does not mention hot work authorization, fire watch, combustible clearance, shielding, or post-work inspection.
The safety board had an outdated lockout/tagout training roster posted. No servicing, maintenance, machine access, or employee exposure to hazardous energy was occurring at the time of observation.
Workers were on a scaffold platform and one side appeared to have a top rail but no midrail. The photo does not show platform height, access ladder, toe boards, or whether fall protection was used.

A worker was working in a 5-foot deep excavation trench. A structural extension ladder was secured inside the shoring box directly next to the worker, requiring less than 5 feet of lateral travel to egress.
A shallow trench, measured at 3 feet deep, was excavated along the perimeter. No employees entered the excavation, and no work tasks were being performed inside the trench.

The die opening measured four inches, the light curtain had been physically removed and lay on the floor beside the machine, and both hands of the operator entered the opening on each of the six strokes observed.
